categories.possible_mechanism: A possible pattern in which a small amount of thinking or physical effort is followed by exhaustion that shows up across more than one part of daily life.

sources.name: Cellular energy and prolonged symptoms after concussion (research article)

who_to_raise_with.adult: A sports medicine physician can help you write down how effort and energy line up, so a GP can look at that pattern with you. This is a conversation about what you notice, not a treatment plan.
who_to_raise_with.teen: A sports medicine physician can help a parent or guardian write down how effort and energy line up, so a pediatric clinician can look at that pattern. This is a conversation about what the teen notices, not a treatment plan.

categories.teen_note: Teen-specific content for this pattern is pending clinician review.

categories.possible_mechanism: A possible pattern in which symptoms show up within minutes of physical activity or a rise in heart rate.

who_to_raise_with.adult: A sports medicine physician can help you describe symptoms that show up with activity or a faster heart rate, so a GP can decide what to review. This visit does not set an exercise plan.
who_to_raise_with.teen: A sports medicine physician can help a parent or guardian describe symptoms that show up with activity, so a pediatric clinician can decide what to review. This visit does not set an exercise plan.

categories.teen_note: Teen-specific content for this pattern is pending clinician review.

categories.possible_mechanism: A possible pattern that can look like sleep trouble, unexplained weight change, or mood shifts that are hard to account for.

sources.name: Hormonal change after traumatic brain injury (research article)

who_to_raise_with.adult: A sleep specialist or a psychologist can help you list sleep and mood changes so a GP can decide whether a hormone check belongs in the conversation. This is not a diagnosis.
who_to_raise_with.teen: A sleep specialist or a psychologist can help a parent or guardian list sleep and mood changes so a pediatric clinician can decide what belongs in the conversation. This is not a diagnosis.

categories.teen_note: Teen-specific content for this pattern is pending clinician review.

categories.possible_mechanism: A possible pattern in which crowds, visual movement, or motion bring on dizziness, disorientation, or nausea.

sources.name: Ontario concussion guideline: vestibular, balance, and vision

who_to_raise_with.adult: A vestibular physiotherapist can help you describe dizziness, motion, and busy places so a GP can see that pattern. The visit is for those details, not a treatment protocol.
who_to_raise_with.teen: A vestibular physiotherapist can help a parent or guardian describe a teen's dizziness and motion symptoms so a pediatric clinician can see that pattern. The visit is for those details, not a treatment protocol.

categories.teen_note: Teen-specific content for this pattern is pending clinician review. Adult guideline claims are not applied to teens.
categories.review_note: Balance and eye-tracking are separate paths in this demo so the survey can tell them apart. That split is pending clinician review.

categories.possible_mechanism: A possible pattern in which reading, screens, scrolling, or following a moving target brings on eye strain or other symptoms.

sources.name: Ontario concussion guideline: vestibular, balance, and vision

who_to_raise_with.adult: A vision therapist can help you describe reading strain, screens, and tracking so a GP can see that pattern. The visit does not start a vision-therapy protocol.
who_to_raise_with.teen: A vision therapist can help a parent or guardian describe a teen's reading strain, screens, and tracking so a pediatric clinician can see that pattern. The visit does not start a vision-therapy protocol.

categories.teen_note: Teen-specific content for this pattern is pending clinician review. Adult guideline claims are not applied to teens.
categories.review_note: Eye-tracking is shown separately from balance so the survey can tell them apart. That split is pending clinician review.

categories.possible_mechanism: A possible pattern of neck tenderness, tension headaches, or strong reactions to light or sound.

sources.name: Clinic explainer on dizziness and vision after concussion

who_to_raise_with.adult: A physiotherapist can help you describe neck tenderness and sensitivity to light or sound so a GP can decide what that pattern means. The visit does not treat the neck as the cause.
who_to_raise_with.teen: A physiotherapist can help a parent or guardian describe a teen's neck tenderness and sensitivity to light or sound so a pediatric clinician can review it. The visit does not treat the neck as the cause.

categories.teen_note: Teen-specific content for this pattern is pending clinician review.
